messages.content: "Could you please help me with some information? First, I would like to know the amount of calories in the 'Chicken Alfredo' recipe from the 'AllRecipes' website for dinner. Second, I am interested in the current stock prices of 'Apple', 'Microsoft', and 'Tesla'. Lastly, I want to know the FIFA ranking of the 'Brazil' men's soccer team in 2018."

function.name: get_stock_price
function.description: Retrieves the current stock price of the specified companies Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

company_names.description: The list of companies for which to retrieve the stock price.

function.name: get_team_ranking
function.description: Retrieve the FIFA ranking of a specific soccer team for a certain year. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

team_name.description: The name of the soccer team.

year.description: The year for which the ranking is to be retrieved.

gender.description: The gender of the team. It can be either 'men' or 'women'. Default is 'men'.

function.name: recipe_info_get_calories
function.description: Retrieve the amount of calories from a specific recipe in a food website. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

website.description: The food website that has the recipe.

optional_meal_time.description: Specific meal time of the day for the recipe (optional, could be 'Breakfast', 'Lunch', 'Dinner'). Default is 'Dinner'

message.reasoning: The user wants three pieces of information. We have three tools: get_team_ranking, get_stock_price, recipe_info_get_calories. We need to call each tool. The user wants the FIFA ranking of Brazil men's soccer team in 2018. That is get_team_ranking with team_name: "Brazil", year: 2018, gender: "men". Then we need the current stock prices of Apple, Microsoft, Tesla. That is get_stock_price with company_names: ["Apple", "Microsoft", "Tesla"]. Then we need the calories of Chicken Alfredo from AllRecipes for dinner. That is recipe_info_get_calories with website: "AllRecipes", recipe: "Chicken Alfredo", optional_meal_time: "Dinner". We need to call each tool separately. The user wants all three. We can do them in separate calls. The user wants the FIFA ranking first, then stock prices, then calories. So we should call get_team_ranking first. Then get_stock_price. Then recipe_info_get_calories.
